rules.heading: Gate every PR on checks that need no credential, and name what is not gated
rules.nativeFeature: Managed Code Review check run (neutral conclusion, never blocks merging)
rules.evidence: The hosted reviewer "always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging through branch protection rules," so a credential-free required gate plus a named list of gaps is posture the harness does not supply.

rules.heading: Give a workflow read-only permissions and pin every action by SHA
rules.nativeFeature: /install-github-app quick setup and manual GitHub Action setup (workflow files pushed into .github/workflows/)
rules.evidence: The setup command "pushes a branch with chosen workflow files, and opens a PR to add them," so the harness puts workflows in the repo without itself constraining their permissions block or pinning the actions they call.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: the rendered `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` ships the read-only default and the SHA pins; copy it when you add a workflow. A workflow the agent platform's own setup command installs is a workflow in this repo too, so give it the same permissions block and the same SHA pins rather than merging it as shipped.

rules.heading: Budget Actions minutes as account-wide money
rules.nativeFeature: GitHub Action cost controls (--max-turns, workflow timeouts, concurrency)
rules.evidence: The documented cost controls "are recommendations, not defaults, none is applied unless the workflow author configures it," which is the floor this rule's account-wide budgeting and pause-then-re-enable procedure builds on.

rules.heading: Open an issue instead of failing a scheduled run, and comment out a cron with its reason
rules.evidence: Nothing in the gathered facts governs whether a scheduled workflow should turn red or open an issue, and the only scheduled-run behavior documented is the trigger-eligibility check that "rejects any bot actor unless listed in allowed_bots."

rules.heading: Turn on push protection, head-branch deletion, and grouped dependency updates
rules.evidence: The harness facts cover the Claude GitHub App's own permission set and workflow installation but say nothing about repository secret-scanning push protection, head-branch deletion, or dependency-update grouping.

rules.heading: Make the PR template force a docs-check answer
rules.nativeFeature: Code Review customization via CLAUDE.md (stale-docs findings capped at nit severity)
rules.evidence: The hosted reviewer reads CLAUDE.md and "treats newly introduced violations as nit-level findings," flagging outdated docs bidirectionally but never requiring an answer, so the template is what makes the docs check mandatory.

rules.heading: Never put a closing keyword beside an issue number you do not mean to close
rules.evidence: No gathered fact describes the harness reading, writing, or warning about closing keywords in a pull request body; PR creation is described only as "you can create pull requests by asking Claude directly."

rules.heading: Ship phased work as commits on one PR
rules.nativeFeature: Background-session git policy (commit, push, draft PR) and /batch parallel worktree automation
rules.evidence: A background session "commits without asking, and pushes the branch when the repository has a remote" and opens a draft PR "when the task calls for it," while /batch "spawns one background subagent per unit in an isolated git worktree" that "opens a pull request," so the single-PR shape has to be stated before work is dispatched that way.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: none (because PR granularity is a judgment call, and the base-retarget confirmation is a look at the open PR list). A background session commits, pushes, and opens a draft pull request on its own, and the parallel-change command opens one per unit, so say which shape phased work takes before dispatching it that way.

rules.heading: Stage explicit paths, never everything at once
rules.evidence: A Bash rule's "* matches any text including spaces" and matches only the command form typically produced, so a rule wide enough to allow staging cannot distinguish a path from a sweep, exactly as the Anchor line already states.

rules.heading: Classify a merged branch by its PR state, not by merge detection
rules.nativeFeature: Periodic worktree cleanup sweep and claude rm unpushed-commit refusal
rules.evidence: The sweep leaves a worktree in place when it "still holds changed/untracked files or unpushed commits" and claude rm blocks on commits "not reachable from the local default branch," which is local state and cannot confirm or refute a squash merge.

rules.heading: Never delete the branch from the worktree being merged
rules.evidence: On exit "a clean, unnamed session auto-removes the worktree and its branch" and a named or dirty one prompts, so any deletion ordered before that point is still the caller's to sequence, as the Anchor line says.

rules.heading: Keep credentials out of the repo, the commit, and the chat
rules.nativeFeature: Sandbox credential protection (deny/mask) and default sandbox filesystem read scope
rules.evidence: "There is no built-in credential deny list, only explicitly listed files/vars are protected," and the default sandbox read scope "still includes credential files like ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/," which is the floor the Anchor line already names.

rules.heading: Scan the built output after scrubbing the build, and plant a canary to prove the scanner fires
rules.evidence: "Sandboxed Bash inherits the parent process's environment variables (including credentials) by default unless sandbox.credentials or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB strips them," so a build started from a session carries the session environment unless scrubbed.

rules.heading: Give a restricted key exactly one writable scope
rules.evidence: No gathered fact governs how a vendor API key is scoped or probed; the nearest item is the Claude GitHub App's fixed permission set, which is a platform app rather than a key this rule issues.

rules.heading: Never log a vendor object
rules.evidence: Nothing in the gathered facts constrains what application code logs; the only related native behavior is egress-side credential masking to listed hosts, which never inspects log payload shape.

rules.heading: Treat a preview URL as production for exposure
rules.evidence: The facts cover network egress allowlisting for sandboxed commands but say nothing about deployed preview hosts or route-level auth policy, so there is no native counterpart to lean on.

rules.heading: Label a non-secret as a non-secret
rules.evidence: The nearest native behavior judges credential-like files by name when bundling a repo to a cloud session and never reads an in-file justification, so labeling a public value is an editorial practice with no harness equivalent.

rules.heading: Ship the community files the platform looks for, and keep issue intake as forms
rules.evidence: The harness reads project instruction files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md but no gathered fact touches a code of conduct, a security policy, a contributing guide, or issue-form intake.

notes: Three calls I was unsure about. (1) "Give a restricted key exactly one writable scope": I marked it UNIQUE, but there is a real adjacent fact worth considering for a future reword, namely that the Claude GitHub App has "a single permission set covering all of its features" and "GitHub doesn't let you accept a subset" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions). That app is the one credential in this repo's orbit that cannot be given one writable scope, so it may deserve naming as a stated gap rather than treated as an exception nobody wrote down. I left it UNIQUE because the rule is about vendor keys the owner issues, not about a platform app whose scopes are fixed by the vendor. (2) "Label a non-secret as a non-secret": the cloud-bundling exclusion of credential-like files (.env, *.tfvars, id_rsa, *.pem) is name-based, not content-based, so a value labeled public in such a file is still withheld from an upload. I could not tell from the facts whether .env.example matches that name pattern, so I did not turn the interaction into a reword. (3) "Ship phased work as commits on one PR" sits closest to CONFLICT of anything in the file, because the parallel-change command opens a pull request per unit by design. I settled on COMPLEMENT since that command targets independent units and requires plan approval, while this rule governs phases of one change; the reword makes the boundary explicit instead of leaving the reader to infer it. Two other Anchor lines already carry accurate native-floor sentences and needed no change: the worktree-sweep claim in "Classify a merged branch by its PR state" is correct for the sweep itself even though agent view does query the platform for a PR-status label, and the hosted-review claims under the gating and PR-template rules match the documented neutral check and nit-level stale-docs finding. No rule in this file duplicates a native floor, and none contradicts one.
